narratives.text:
Tallink Grupp reported strong Q1 2024 results with revenue of EUR 210.4 million, representing 8% year-on-year growth. The increase was primarily driven by higher passenger volumes on the Tallinn-Helsinki route and improved cargo operations.

EBITDA reached EUR 48.7 million with margins expanding to 23.1%, reflecting operational efficiency gains and successful cost management initiatives across all routes. Net profit of EUR 12.3 million marked a return to profitability after a challenging Q1 2023.

The company maintained a solid balance sheet position with total assets of EUR 1.65 billion and equity of EUR 890 million, providing a strong foundation for future growth investments.

CEO Paavo Nõgene commented: 'Our Q1 performance demonstrates the resilience of our business model and the dedication of our team. We continue to invest in fleet modernization and digital services to enhance the customer experience.'

Management highlighted the successful launch of the new online booking platform and the positive customer response to the upgraded onboard services. The company remains focused on operational efficiency and sustainability initiatives.

Management expects continued recovery in passenger numbers through 2024, driven by tourism growth in the Baltic region and the normalization of travel patterns post-pandemic. However, fuel price volatility and geopolitical uncertainty in the Baltic Sea region remain key risk factors.

The company plans to maintain its current capacity levels while optimizing route profitability. Capital expenditure for 2024 is projected at EUR 45-50 million, focused on vessel maintenance and digitalization projects.

sentiment.outlook: Management expects continued recovery in passenger numbers through 2024, with potential headwinds from fuel price volatility and geopolitical uncertainty.
